articles.title: Why a card printing business built three free tools
articles.excerpt: We supply custom-printed plastic cards to businesses around New Zealand: gift and loyalty cards, membership and staff ID, hotel keys, and RFID and NFC cards. The work is mostly B2B, often through prin…
articles.body: We supply custom-printed plastic cards to businesses around New Zealand: gift and loyalty cards, membership and staff ID, hotel keys, and RFID and NFC cards. The work is mostly B2B, often through print companies and brokers, and a lot of it depends on a file someone else has prepared. After enough jobs, the pattern was familiar. The delay was rarely the print itself. It was the artwork. A file would arrive at the wrong finished size — often a paper business-card format — or with no bleed, or with a logo sitting where the magnetic stripe has to go. A QR code would look crisp on screen and then fail on a phone once it was 15 millimetres wide on a glossy card. We check every file before it goes to print, and we should — a bad file should never become a bad run of cards.

articles.title: 셀시우스의 진짜 붕괴: 단순한 시장 전염병 그 이상의 이야기

articles.body: 서론 헤드라인들은 시장 전염병, 테라/루나 붕괴, 그리고 뒤이은 쓰리애로우즈캐피탈(3AC)의 몰락에 대해 소리쳤다. 이 외부적 충격들이 셀시우스 네트워크가 파산으로 치닫게 된 주된 원인이라고 지목했지. 2022년 6월 12일, 셀시우스가 갑작스레 모든 고객의 출금, 이체, 스왑을 중단했을 때, 즉각적인 반응은 암호화폐 시장을 휩쓴 연쇄적인 실패들을 탓하는 것이었다. 하지만 이 바닥을 30년간 지켜본 사람으로서 말해주자면, 그런 외부 사건들은 분명 강력한 촉매제였지만, 셀시우스 몰락의 진짜 원인은 아니었어. 내가 보기엔 셀시우스 실패의 진짜 시작점은 훨씬 더 깊은 곳에 있었다. 그것은 리스크에 대한 근본적인 왜곡이었고, 지속 가능한 고수익이라는 환상 위에 세워진 위험천만한 사업 모델이었다. 새 시대의 블록체인 옷을 입었을 뿐, '탈중앙화'나 '투명성'의 의미를 제대로 이해하지 못한 구시대적 금융 차익거래 방식이었던 셈이다. 알렉스 마신스키의 지휘 아래, 회사는 사용자들에게 예치금에 대해 최대 17%에 달하는 수익률을 약속했다. 기관 대출자에게 자산을 빌려주고 디파이(DeFi) 전략에 참여하여 이러한 수익을 창출한다고 주장했지. 내가 보기에 문제는 단순히 무엇에 투자했느냐가 아니라, 어떻게 운영했느냐, 그리고 그 약속들의 내재된 취약성이었다. 여기서 핵심은 간단하다. 셀시우스는 갑작스럽고 예측 불가능한 시장 이벤트 때문에 무너진 게 아니라는 거다. 그것은 시한폭탄과 같았다. 시장 상황이 변하면 터지도록 설계되어 있었지.

articles.title: 整理脏数据，不要吝啬模型算力和 Token
articles.excerpt: 先说结论 处理一堆脏数据时，我现在更愿意先把模型能力、上下文和执行条件给足，而不是自己坐下来设计分类。尤其是大量杂乱文档的整理，真正困难的地方不是改几个标题、挪几个位置，而是要先理解所有内容，再判断它们应该怎样组织、哪些信息互相关联。 过去总觉得整理数据是简单劳动，用便宜模型就可以。实际效果不好，又以为问题在于自己没有先把结构设计清楚。现在重新想，这个判断可能一开始就错了：不是所有整理工作都适合用…
articles.body: 先说结论 处理一堆脏数据时，我现在更愿意先把模型能力、上下文和执行条件给足，而不是自己坐下来设计分类。尤其是大量杂乱文档的整理，真正困难的地方不是改几个标题、挪几个位置，而是要先理解所有内容，再判断它们应该怎样组织、哪些信息互相关联。 过去总觉得整理数据是简单劳动，用便宜模型就可以。实际效果不好，又以为问题在于自己没有先把结构设计清楚。现在重新想，这个判断可能一开始就错了：不是所有整理工作都适合用低成本模型做。 数据越脏、越缺少明确规则，越可能需要更强的推理能力。 我曾经把整理文档当成简单任务 最近整理自己的 ChatGPT Space 资料库时，面对一大堆杂乱文档，常常不知道从哪里下手。文档多了，不只是内容需要修改，还涉及分类、归属、关联关系，以及不同资料应该如何一起维护。 我之前的想法很简单：让 AI 去做这些整理工作，应该不难，所以没有必要在模型和 Token 上花太多成本。结果整理出来的效果不理想。后来甚至开始反思，是不是应该先由自己确定整个目录架构，让 AI 按照人的分类去执行。 这个思路看起来很稳妥，却忽略了另一个可能性： 如果交给 AI 的本来就是一件复杂的理解任务，我却一直用低配置的方式去做，那么问题未必出在分类方法上。 脏数据最难的部分，恰恰是还没有规则 一份结构化、格式统一的数据，字段是什么意思、怎样归类、需要转换成什么样，往往都很明确。这样的工作交给脚本或者便宜模型就能处理，甚至不一定需要大模型。 但杂乱文档不是这样。它们可能来自不同时间、不同项目，表达方式不一致；有的内容是在记录过去的决定，有的是目前正在执行的规则，还有的只是一个没有展开的想法。AI 需要先判断每份材料是什么，再综合其他材料理解它的用途。 也就是说，干净数据通常是在执行规则；脏数据可能需要先发现规则、建立结构，再执行规则。后者看上去像整理杂物，实际上包含不少理解和推理。 以前恰恰在这…

articles.excerpt: CSS makes custom cursors look like one line of code. Browsers add several rules that make them fail silently. https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/cursor); W3C, CSS Basic User Interface Le…
articles.body: CSS makes custom cursors look like one line of code. Browsers add several rules that make them fail silently. The syntax .my-area { cursor: url("pointer.cur"), auto; } The final keyword is required as the fallback. The rules 128 px maximum. Chrome and Firefox refuse larger cursor images. 32 px is the practical size. Chrome hides cursors bigger than 32 px when they touch its own interface, and MDN recommends 32 x 32. Multi-size .cur files backfire. Chrome and Firefox use the largest image, so a Windows-style file with 128 px inside shows a huge pointer. Setting the click point Two ways.

articles.title: How to add collision to a Godot TileMapLayer (and an AI that did it in 2 minutes)
articles.excerpt: This post is the collision section of our full guide, Godot TileMapLayer Tutorial: Setup & Example Project, where you can download the example project used below. A TileMapLayer has no collision until…
articles.body: This post is the collision section of our full guide, Godot TileMapLayer Tutorial: Setup & Example Project , where you can download the example project used below. Add collision to a TileMapLayer A TileMapLayer has no collision until its TileSet has a physics layer and the solid tiles have collision polygons. The steps, from the official TileSet tutorial : Select the TileMapLayer, click its TileSet property in the inspector, unfold Physics Layers and choose Add Element . Open the TileSet editor at the bottom, select a solid tile and open its Physics Layer 0 section. Press F for a full-tile rectangle, or draw a polygon. Repeat for every solid tile. Tiles without a polygon stay walk-through, which is what you want for water or decoration.

articles.title: A Texas county's tax rate was doubled in the state file, and two of my three checks passed it
articles.excerpt: The Texas Comptroller publishes a spreadsheet with the tax rate of all 254 counties and a second one with more than 4,800 local taxing units. I use both to estimate property tax bills, so a wrong rate…
articles.body: The Texas Comptroller publishes a spreadsheet with the tax rate of all 254 counties and a second one with more than 4,800 local taxing units. I use both to estimate property tax bills, so a wrong rate turns directly into a wrong number on a page. The 2025 county file says Fort Bend County's rate is $0.824 per $100 of taxable value. The rate the county actually adopted is $0.412 . On a home with $300,000 of taxable value, that is a $1,236 difference in the county line of the bill. The file is labeled "Working" and dated 01/28/2026, so this isn't a complaint about the Comptroller. It's a report built from what thousands of local units submit. But it is the kind of error a data pipeline will happily carry through, and the interesting part is which checks catch it.

articles.title: Can AI fix a ChatGPT-made Godot shader? We tested Ziva on a real forum shader
articles.excerpt: This post is one section of our full guide, Godot Shaders in 2026: A Practical Guide to GDShader. A chat assistant can write GDShader, but it cannot compile what it writes. You paste the code into God…
articles.body: This post is one section of our full guide, Godot Shaders in 2026: A Practical Guide to GDShader . Tested: an AI fixing a ChatGPT-made shader in the editor A chat assistant can write GDShader, but it cannot compile what it writes. You paste the code into Godot, copy the error back, and repeat. An agent inside the editor can compile each change and look at the running scene. We tested that loop with Ziva on a real broken shader. The shader comes from a Godot forum post from December 2025 (Godot 4.5). Its author "made the individual parts with the help of ChatGPT" and stitched them into one canvas_item shader: background removal, blur, an overlay texture and color correction. With every module at its default, the sprite came out "much more contrasty" and lost "a lot of brightness".

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 9, 1967: NASA launches the Saturn V moon rocket for the first time on Apollo 4, but no astronauts were aboard
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Nov. 9, 1967: NASA launches the Saturn V moon rocket for the first time on Apollo 4, but no astronauts were aboard
articles.body: On Nov. 9, 1967, NASA launched the powerful new Saturn V rocket on its maiden voyage. The Saturn V moon rocket was 363 feet tall. That's taller than the Statue of Liberty! It was the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built at the time (though SpaceX's Starship megarocket has since surpassed it). NASA needed such a powerful rocket to launch astronauts to the moon. However, the first Saturn V launch didn't carry astronauts, because it was only a test flight. During the launch, the rocket created a loud shockwave that surprised nearby observers. The ground shook so hard that it rattled buildings miles away, and all the shaking caused a huge shower of dust and debris NASA's new launch center, the Kennedy Space Center in Florida. The mission lasted 8 hours 36 minutes.

articles.title: Jupiter and Mars are set for a breathtaking close approach later this week: Here's how to see it
articles.excerpt: Jupiter and Mars will appear incredibly close as they shine in the constellation Leo on Nov. 15.
articles.body: Jupiter and Mars will shine side by side in a spectacular close approach in the heart of the constellation Leo on Nov. 15. Here's what you need to know. Mars and Jupiter reach their closest apparent separation in Earth's sky at 9:04 p.m. EST on Nov. 15 (0204 GMT on Nov. 16), according to astronomy website In-The-Sky . The planets will be below the horizon for U.S. stargazers at the moment of their closest approach, but observers can catch the pair rising above the eastern horizon around midnight local time, just a few hours later. Remember: You can discover the exact timings for the rising and setting of the planets above your local horizon using Time and Date's night sky tracker .

articles.title: Are the James Webb Space Telescope's mysterious Little Red Dots actually tiny black holes left over from the Big Bang era?
articles.excerpt: New research suggests that Little Red Dots, which have puzzled astronomers since the JWST began discovering them, could host primordial black holes born during the Big Bang.
articles.body: Ever since NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) started observing the early universe, it has been providing almost as many surprises as it has answers. One such surprise are the so-called Little Red Dots, cosmic objects that seemingly disappear completely before the universe is two billion years old. New research suggests that Little Red Dots may actually be connected primordial black holes , tiny black holes born not from dying stars but rather from fluctuations in the density of matter just after the Big Bang, in the earliest moments of cosmic history. Should they exist, primordial black holes would predate stars, galactic dust particles, and elements heavier than hydrogen and helium.

articles.title: Vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices is under active exploitation
articles.excerpt: "*sshole" poses a serious threat to Internet security.
articles.body: Hackers are actively exploiting a recently discovered critical vulnerability that allows them to log in to privileged accounts on many Linux systems, multiple researchers are reporting. The vulnerability, tracked under the name *sshole, arises from the interaction between OpenSSH and a code library known as musl. Linux systems that use both of these packages and meet certain other requirements can be hacked to give unauthenticated access to high-privilege accounts in a matter of seconds. *sshole became publicly known last Thursday and quickly stoked concerns it could lead to widespread compromise of Linux machines. Four days later, the prediction shows signs of becoming real.
